rationale: Full English article read (1,027 lines). Concrete face-up creature cards and energy tokens identify the trading-card game. Official replay logs feed behavior cloning, visible board information feeds legal-option ranking, a validated rule fallback joins the same decision surface, and the policy is evaluated in full games. This highlights the article's distinction between offline imitation accuracy and full-game pilot strength. Offline RL and population self-play remain planned in the article, so no completed RL loop, reward chart, benchmark score, or claimed win improvement is depicted.
alt_en: Replay-based behavior cloning and a rule fallback rank legal trading-card choices from the visible board before full-game evaluation.
alt_ko: 리플레이로 학습한 행동 모방 모델과 규칙 기반 대안이 공개된 카드판을 보고 합법적 선택지를 평가하며, 이후 전체 게임으로 파일럿을 검증한다.
prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: professional technical blog cover for a Pokémon trading-card game AI working note, wide landscape approximately 1.9:1.
Primary request: clearly show a card-game pilot that learns from replays, ranks the currently legal choices, retains a rule fallback, and is tested in complete games. This is a concrete technical architecture for trading-card decisions, not a fantasy battle poster and not an abstract essay illustration.
Main scene: at left, a small neat tabletop showing a face-up active creature trading card, a partially visible benched creature card, and two small attached-energy counters. The illustrated card portraits can be simple original friendly monster shapes, one ghost-like and one insect-like, rendered as restrained flat line art. The cards have no printed name, HP, damage, attack cost, rules text, or numbers; they are schematic, not replicas of real card faces. A visible-board arrow leads into a central clean legal-choice menu with three rows labelled "Attach", "Attack", and "Switch". Show a short unnumbered blue ranking bar in each row, and highlight one chosen legal row in teal; do not claim it is optimal or a winning move. To the right, show two modest facing card mats and a checklist icon for full-game evaluation, without a score, trophy, result chart, or victory indicator.
Learning and safety architecture: a secondary upper row contains a small replay-log stack labelled "Replays" feeding a compact "Behavior cloning" model block, with a downward arrow into the central menu's ranker. A secondary lower "Rule fallback" block connects into that same central decision point, showing a safe alternative when model coverage or confidence is low. Both learning and fallback rank only choices already supplied by the engine. The training row is separate from the runtime visible-board flow.
Text (verbatim), only these nine short labels: "Replays", "Behavior cloning", "Visible board", "Legal-option ranking", "Attach", "Attack", "Switch", "Rule fallback", "Full-game evaluation". No long title or other text.
Concept accuracy: the article is about variable-length legal-option ranking under partial observability, BC followed by hybrid rule/model pilots, faithful opponents, temporal evaluation, and an untouched holdout. BC is supervised imitation, not reinforcement learning; offline RL and population self-play are still planned, so do not draw a completed PPO/RL feedback loop, reward curve, success badge, or claimed improvement. Do not show hidden opponent cards being fed into the model. Do not display invented win rates or card statistics, and do not depict a fixed class head tied permanently to action index.
Style/medium: polished flat technical editorial diagram, crisp slate #334A5A linework and simple concrete card/table/model objects, white/off-white #F7F8F7 background, restrained teal #488A8A and blue #658CB2. Very small muted creature-colour accents are acceptable, but no vivid trading-card foil, glossy 3D, painterly grain, fireworks, saturated fantasy background, or decorative network mesh.
Composition/framing: wide horizontal 1.9:1 cover for 1200-by-630 blog display; a balanced readable main left-to-right flow with compact upper learning branch and lower fallback branch, generous whitespace and safe central margins. English labels must be large and clean. No logo, copyrighted card graphics, brand wordmark, watermark, border, dense code, or screenshot UI. Deliver one finished technical cover.
quality_review: Generated source and final WebP inspected: legible labels, concrete cards and current choices, no invented card names/HP/damage, no hidden-opponent-state input, separate BC training and runtime flow, rule fallback, full-game evaluation without scores.
